about_your_time.body: The Zapier agent went through three delivery methods — Zapier MCP, manual send, then Apps Script — before it had a version that runs without you. The Obsidian connector took five rounds of config debugging. You don't drop the thread when the first path fails.
about_your_time.title: You keep pushing past the first answer.

about_your_time.body: ManageCafe's PRD got divided between you and Jayesh twice in the same day, and you started the frontend build that night with a 9 AM deadline.
about_your_time.title: You split work with your team, then build your half fast.

about_your_time.body: The DSA roadmap wasn't a topic list — you asked for Obsidian notes, cross-day connections, and a constraint that every problem's optimal solution uses only that day's technique.
about_your_time.title: You want the system, not just the lesson.

expanding_your_skills.body: ManageCafe's frontend code came from Claude, and so did the DSA problem sets — but you chose the overnight build order yourself, and you came back with your own solution to LeetCode 1480 before moving to Day 2.
expanding_your_skills.title: You hand off the generation, but you decide what ships.

expanding_your_skills.body: The DSA request opened with four rules: explain to a 15-year-old, 30 years of teaching experience, visual format, and only problems solvable with that day's topic. The monthly report started with "keep exactly the same format as the docx file."
expanding_your_skills.title: Constraints come first in how you set up a task.

expanding_your_skills.body: You caught the missing return statement in your LeetCode 1480 solution after Claude confirmed the logic was correct, and you pushed back on the Zapier agent when no email arrived the next morning.
expanding_your_skills.title: You notice when the tool gives you something that doesn't run.

expanding_your_skills.body: Most conversations focused on generating code and research rather than on how AI-assisted work gets represented downstream. Nothing to build on yet.
expanding_your_skills.title: There wasn't enough this month to reflect on this skill.

content.hero_body: ManageCafe, the WhatsApp clone, the DSA roadmap, the monthly report, the daily tech-research agent — each one started as a single ask and turned into a multi-step build. You used Claude as a researcher and a code generator, but the pattern underneath was consistent: you'd define what you wanted, get the structure back, then push for the version that actually runs. The Zapier-to-Apps-Script pivot and the Obsidian MCP config debug both followed the same arc — hit a wall, stay in the conversation, find the working path.
content.hero_title: Building things, then building the system around them.
